primary_paper.title: Mussel Inspired Hydrogel Promotes Axon Regeneration via Piezo1 Modulation and Cytoskeleton Dynamics in Synergy After Spinal Cord Injury

developmental_mechanics.method: atomic force microscopy of uninjured rat spinal cord across neonatal, young and adult stages
developmental_mechanics.interpretation: The paper directly links a developmental rise in spinal-cord stiffness to the age axis on which axonal regenerative competence declines, but does not by itself prove that stiffness is the sole developmental cause of that decline.

causal_in_vivo_intervention.animal: female Sprague-Dawley rat, approximately 6 weeks old
causal_in_vivo_intervention.hydrogel_family: same catechol-modified methacrylated hyaluronic-acid platform with polymer concentration varied to tune stiffness
causal_in_vivo_intervention.key_result: the softer neonatal-like HAMA@CA condition reduced lesion-region elasticity toward approximately 300 Pa and produced smaller cavities, more axonal growth, myelination/synaptic structures and better functional recovery than stiffer/control conditions
causal_in_vivo_intervention.timing: implantation at the time of transection

mechanotransduction.in_vitro_stiffness_response: stiffer matrices increased Piezo1/RhoA/cytoskeletal restraint and reduced axon elongation; softer matrices increased branching/elongation

pharmacology.result: pharmacological manipulation shifted downstream RhoA/p-MLC/MLC2 in the predicted direction

independent_spinal_cord_replication.paper: Biomaterial scaffold stiffness influences the foreign body reaction, tissue stiffness, angiogenesis and neuroregeneration in spinal cord injury
independent_spinal_cord_replication.model: adult rat C5 lateral hemisection with stiffness-varied alginate anisotropic capillary hydrogel scaffolds
independent_spinal_cord_replication.result: scaffold stiffness changed host foreign-body reaction, YAP-associated mechanosensing, tissue mechanics, angiogenesis and axonal regrowth; mechanically matched/soft formulations were favored for integration/regrowth, although growth orientation showed trade-offs

directional_falsifier.paper: The influence of hydrogel stiffness on axonal regeneration after spinal cord injury
directional_falsifier.finding: 15% GelMA produced better axonal extension and sensory functional recovery than 7.5% GelMA in that complete-transection model
directional_falsifier.meaning: A universal monotonic rule SOFTER_IS_ALWAYS_MORE_REGENERATIVE is falsified; optimal mechanics are material-, scale-, geometry- and tissue-state-dependent.

confound_audit.reason: HAMA@CA stiffness was tuned by changing polymer concentration; this can also affect polymer density, swelling, degradation, transport and adhesion even though chemistry and gross channel architecture were shared.

gate_verdict.reason: Developmental spinal-cord stiffening is directly measured, adult lesion stiffening is measured, and mechanically retuning the injured niche changes regeneration and function. However, polymer concentration and adhesion remain coupled to stiffness and the intervention begins immediately after injury.

next_killer_tests: same-chemistry, same-architecture, same-adhesion scaffold series in which modulus is varied independently of polymer concentration
delayed softening or mechanical retuning initiated after the adult lesion/scar mechanical state is established
dense AFM plus axon-growth time series to determine whether mechanical retuning precedes the regeneration shift
in-vivo Piezo1-pathway necessity test under matched mechanical conditions
